events.title: Birth of Horatio Nelson
events.description: Horatio Nelson, the future British naval hero, was born in Burnham Thorpe, Norfolk. He rose through the Royal Navy to become one of its most celebrated admirals.
events.significance: Nelson's tactical daring secured British naval dominance during the Napoleonic Wars. He died at the 1805 Battle of Trafalgar.

events.title: Babi Yar Massacre Begins
events.description: Nazi forces and their collaborators began a two-day massacre at the Babi Yar ravine outside Kyiv. About 33,000 Jewish people were killed.
events.significance: Babi Yar is one of the largest single mass shootings of the Holocaust. It is remembered as a symbol of Nazi atrocity in occupied Europe.

events.title: CERN Is Established
events.description: The European Organization for Nuclear Research was formally established, after twelve European governments ratified its founding convention.
events.significance: CERN became a model of international scientific cooperation. It is home to the Large Hadron Collider and the birthplace of the World Wide Web.

events.title: Canada Launches Alouette 1
events.description: Canada's first satellite, Alouette 1, lifted off from Vandenberg Air Force Base in California. The joint effort with NASA was built to study the Earth's ionosphere.
events.significance: The launch made Canada the third country to put a satellite into orbit, after the Soviet Union and the United States.

events.title: Sinking of the MS Estonia
events.description: The passenger ferry MS Estonia sank in the Baltic Sea during a storm. More than 800 people died.
events.significance: It was among the deadliest peacetime maritime disasters in European waters. It led to major reviews of ferry safety standards.
